To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the substitution pattern of thermoplastic maize starch laurates depends on the activation of laurate, that the melting temperature of the starch laurates is influenced by the degree of substitution (and thus by the substitution pattern) and by the molar mass and that the solubility is dependent on both the degree of substitution and the molar mass.

thermoplastic starch esters can be prepared by reacting starch with lauric anhydride or lauric acid, and that the properties of the starch ester are influenced by the DS, the degree of branching of the starch and the molar mass.

starch laurates with high degrees of substitution can be synthesized from starch and lauric acid in N,N' dimethylacetamide/LiCl by using 4 toluensulfonyl chloride/N,N' dicyclobexylcarbodiimde/1 pyrrolidinepyridine,1 1 carbonyldiimadazole, or N,N dimethyl formamide/oxalyl chloride as activator.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of thermoplastic, biodegradable starch laurates with improved processability and properties for applications in food and nonfood packaging.
the synthesis of new thermoplastic starch derivatives with different properties.
the synthesis of new biodegradable thermoplastic starch esters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the activation of laurates with DMF in the presence of oxalyl chloride gives the best results.
thermoplastic starch esters can be prepared in a simple way by reacting starch with lauric or palmitic acid.
the reaction efficiency is the most important parameter for the synthesis of thermoplastic esters of starch.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
thermoplastic starch esters with a DS of 1.0 are soluble in chloroform, dichloromethane and tetrahydrofuran.
thermoplastic starch esters are a versatile class of biodegradable polymers.
thermoplastic starch esters are a promising class of biodegradable materials for use in packaging, coating, and molding applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activation of the acid with DMF and oxalyl chloride is a very efficient and mild method for the homogeneous synthesis of thermoplastic esters of starch.
thermoplastic starches with high DS and high molar mass can be prepared in homogeneous solution.
the substitution pattern and the DS of starch laurates can be tailored by varying the activation agent.
